semantic_correction.stem: A client using subcutaneous insulin glargine repeatedly injects into the same thickened, lumpy area because it is less painful. Which teaching is most appropriate?

options.A: Avoid the abnormal area, rotate sites within the chosen region, and monitor glucose closely when moving to unaffected tissue.
options.B: Continue using the lumpy area because repeated injections there make insulin absorption more predictable.
options.C: Massage the thickened area after each injection so the insulin is absorbed more rapidly.
options.D: Use the same skin spot for each dose because changing sites increases the risk of lipodystrophy.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current LANTUS labeling instructs patients to rotate injection sites within the same region and not inject into areas of lipodystrophy or localized cutaneous amyloidosis. Repeated injections into affected areas have been associated with hyperglycemia, while a sudden change from affected to unaffected tissue has been associated with hypoglycemia. The label therefore advises changing to unaffected sites under close supervision with increased glucose monitoring. Continuing to inject into abnormal tissue or massaging it does not address the injection-site problem.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach insulin-glargine users to avoid lipodystrophic or lumpy areas, rotate injection sites, and monitor glucose more closely when changing from affected to unaffected tissue.
semantic_correction.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration
semantic_correction.source_version_date: SPL revision May 31, 2025; current DailyMed labeling accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Section 2.1 Important Administration Instructions — rotate injection sites within the same region and do not inject into lipodystrophy/localized cutaneous amyloidosis; Section 5.2 Hyperglycemia or Hypoglycemia with Changes in Insulin Regimen — affected-site hyperglycemia, change-to-unaffected-site hypoglycemia, closer glucose monitoring
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: LANTUS labeling directs site rotation and avoidance of lipodystrophic/amyloid areas and advises close glucose monitoring when patients who repeatedly injected into affected tissue change to unaffected sites.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: made the medication source-specific to insulin glargine, removed the 'only' distractor, shortened the correct answer, and preserved the label's clinically important hypoglycemia risk when moving from abnormal to unaffected tissue.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — parenteral medication safety and teaching
audit_findings_append.finding: The original item was directionally correct but generic despite citing a product label and had a longer correct answer. The revised item explicitly identifies insulin glargine and uses balanced teaching alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It directly applies the LANTUS site-rotation, affected-site avoidance, and increased glucose-monitoring instructions.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Repeated injections into affected tissue have been associated with hyperglycemia rather than predictable absorption.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. The label directs avoidance of affected tissue, not post-injection massage of the abnormal area.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Repeated use of the same spot contributes to injection-site abnormalities; the label directs rotation within the region.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines all source-supported actions required by the scenario.
cueing_check: All four choices are injection-site teaching statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: current DailyMed LANTUS labeling freshly verified
